documents.name: Aardvark
documents.description: Explore the aardvark (Orycteropus afer): a nocturnal, burrowing African mammal that feeds on ants and termites and is the sole living member of its own order.

documents.name: Aardwolf
documents.description: Explore the aardwolf (Proteles cristata): a small, striped, insect-eating member of the hyena family that laps up tens of thousands of termites a night with a long, sticky tongue.

documents.name: Abalone
documents.description: Abalone are large marine gastropods (genus Haliotis) with iridescent, ear-shaped shells. Learn about their algae diet, rocky habitat, and conservation.

documents.name: Adelie Penguin
documents.description: Learn about the Adelie penguin, a small Antarctic seabird that breeds on ice-free coasts, feeds on krill at sea, and is listed as Least Concern.

documents.name: African Buffalo
documents.description: Learn about the African (Cape) buffalo, Syncerus caffer, a large wild bovid of sub-Saharan Africa: appearance, herds, habitat, ecology, and conservation.

documents.name: African Grey Parrot
documents.description: Learn about the African grey parrot (Psittacus erithacus), a rainforest bird known for vocal mimicry and cognition, and why it is listed as Endangered.

documents.name: Agama
documents.description: Explore agamas (genus Agama): bold African rock lizards in which dominant males flush brilliant red-and-blue, doing 'push-ups' to display — using the red-headed rock agama.

documents.name: Agouti
documents.description: Explore agoutis (genus Dasyprocta): long-legged Neotropical rodents that run on tiptoe — and, by burying seeds they later forget, are key planters of rainforest trees like the Brazil nut.

documents.name: Albatross
documents.description: Explore albatrosses (family Diomedeidae): ocean-wandering seabirds with the largest wingspans of any living bird, able to glide vast distances — and among the most threatened birds.

documents.name: Aldabra Giant Tortoise
documents.description: Meet the Aldabra giant tortoise (Aldabrachelys gigantea), a huge long-lived grazing tortoise of Aldabra Atoll, Seychelles. Habitat, diet, ecology and status.

documents.name: Alligator
documents.description: Alligatoridae: alligators of North America and China. Habitats, ambush hunting, parental nest care, and the differences between alligators and crocodiles.

documents.name: Alligator Gar
documents.description: Discover the alligator gar, a large ancient freshwater fish of the southern United States and parts of Mexico, including its biology, habitat and ecology.

documents.name: Alligator Lizard
documents.description: Explore alligator lizards (genus Elgaria and relatives): long-tailed North American lizards with armoured, alligator-like scales and a stretchy skin fold along each side.

documents.name: Alpaca
documents.description: A natural-history profile of the alpaca (Vicugna pacos), the smaller domesticated South American camelid bred for dense fleece, and how it differs from the llama.

documents.name: Alpine Ibex
documents.description: Learn about the Alpine ibex (Capra ibex), a wild goat of the European Alps known for its huge ridged horns, steep rocky habitat, and conservation recovery.

documents.name: Amazonian Giant Centipede
documents.description: Learn about the Amazonian giant centipede (Scolopendra gigantea), a large predatory arthropod of parts of northern South America, its biology and ecology.

documents.name: American Alligator
documents.description: Learn about the American alligator, a large crocodilian of southeastern U.S. wetlands, its biology, ecological role, and conservation recovery story.

documents.name: American Black Bear
documents.description: Learn about the American black bear (Ursus americanus), the most widespread bear in North America: its appearance, forest habitat, diet, and behavior.

documents.name: Amphipod
documents.description: Explore amphipods (order Amphipoda): small, sideways-flattened crustaceans — sandhoppers, scuds, and deep-sea giants — that are abundant recyclers and a vital food source in water worldwide.

documents.name: Amphiuma
documents.description: Explore amphiumas (genus Amphiuma): long, slick, aquatic salamanders of the US Southeast with four absurdly tiny legs — among the longest amphibians in North America, and a serious biter.

documents.name: Anaconda
documents.description: The green anaconda (Eunectes murinus) is one of the world's largest snakes. An educational profile of these aquatic, non-venomous constrictors — habitat, diet, and behaviour.

documents.name: Andean Condor
documents.description: The Andean Condor is a large New World vulture of the Andes and nearby coasts. Learn about its appearance, soaring flight, ecology, and conservation.

documents.name: Angelfish
documents.description: The freshwater angelfish (Pterophyllum scalare): an educational profile of this tall-finned cichlid — appearance, Amazon habitat, behaviour, and aquarium context.

documents.name: Anglerfish
documents.description: Explore deep-sea anglerfish (suborder Ceratioidei): dark-water predators that dangle a glowing, bacteria-powered lure to attract prey, with one of nature's strangest mating systems.

documents.name: Anole
documents.description: Explore anoles (genus Anolis): small, agile American lizards famous for the male's throat fan (dewlap) and a textbook example of rapid evolution — using the green anole as a reference.

documents.name: Ant
documents.description: Ants are social insects living in colonies. A group-level overview of the family Formicidae: castes, nests, varied diets, and ecological importance.

documents.name: Antarctic Krill
documents.description: Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba) is a small swarming crustacean and keystone of the Southern Ocean food web, feeding whales, seals and penguins.

documents.name: Antarctic Toothfish
documents.description: The Antarctic toothfish is a large, slow-growing predatory fish of the Southern Ocean around Antarctica, with antifreeze proteins in its blood.

documents.name: Antlion
documents.description: Explore antlions (family Myrmeleontidae): insects whose larvae dig conical sand pits to trap ants — then transform into delicate, lacewing-like winged adults.

documents.name: Antpitta
documents.description: Explore antpittas (family Grallariidae): plump, almost tailless, long-legged Neotropical birds that hop along the forest floor — elusive 'voices in the undergrowth' beloved by birders.

documents.name: Aphid
documents.description: Explore aphids (family Aphididae): tiny sap-sucking insects that reproduce explosively by cloning, produce sugary honeydew 'milked' by ants, and rank among the top garden pests.

documents.name: Arapaima
documents.description: The arapaima is one of the world's largest freshwater fish, an air-breathing giant of the Amazon basin. Explore its biology, range, and conservation notes.

documents.name: Archerfish
documents.description: Explore archerfish (family Toxotidae): coastal and mangrove fish that knock insects off overhanging plants by spitting precise jets of water — sharpshooters that correct for light refraction.

documents.name: Arctic Fox
documents.description: Learn about the Arctic fox (Vulpes lagopus), a small tundra fox with a color-changing coat, its habitat, diet, behavior, ecology, and conservation.

documents.name: Armadillo
documents.description: Armadillos are armoured digging mammals of the Americas. A group-level overview using the nine-banded armadillo as a reference — habitat, diet, and behaviour.

documents.name: Asian Arowana
documents.description: Learn about the Asian arowana (Scleropages formosus), an Endangered, CITES Appendix I freshwater fish of Southeast Asia prized in the ornamental-fish trade.

documents.name: Asian Black Bear
documents.description: Learn about the Asian black bear (Ursus thibetanus), or moon bear: its crescent chest mark, forest range across parts of Asia, diet, and conservation status.

documents.name: Asian Giant Hornet
documents.description: Learn about the Asian giant hornet (Vespa mandarinia), the world's largest hornet native to parts of East and South Asia, its biology, ecology, and behavior.

documents.name: Asian Giant Salamander
documents.description: Asian giant salamanders (genus Andrias) are the largest living amphibians, fully aquatic dwellers of cool, clear streams in parts of East Asia. Learn the facts.

documents.name: Atlantic Salmon
documents.description: Learn about the Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), an anadromous fish of North Atlantic rivers and seas, including its life cycle, ecology, and conservation.

documents.name: Axolotl
documents.description: Explore the axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum): a neotenic salamander from Mexico City's lakes that keeps its gills for life, famous for regeneration — common in science, critically endangered in the wild.

documents.name: Aye-Aye
documents.description: Explore the aye-aye (Daubentonia madagascariensis): a strange nocturnal lemur of Madagascar that taps wood and fishes out grubs with an elongated middle finger. Endangered.

documents.name: Babirusa
documents.description: Explore babirusas (genus Babyrousa): bizarre wild pigs of Indonesia's Sulawesi region whose males grow upper tusks that pierce through the snout and curve back toward the skull.

documents.name: Baboon
documents.description: Explore baboons (genus Papio): large, ground-living African monkeys with dog-like muzzles, powerful builds, and some of the most complex social lives of any non-human primate.

documents.name: Badger
documents.description: Badgers are stocky, burrowing mammals. A group-level overview using the European badger as a reference species: setts, omnivorous diet, and nocturnal behaviour.

documents.name: Bald Eagle
documents.description: Learn about the bald eagle, a large North American sea eagle with a white head and tail, its habitat, diet, behavior, and notable conservation recovery.

documents.name: Bandicoot
documents.description: Explore bandicoots (order Peramelemorphia): small, pointy-snouted, omnivorous marsupials of Australia and New Guinea — busy diggers using the long-nosed bandicoot as a reference.

documents.name: Barbet
documents.description: Explore barbets: stout, vividly coloured tropical birds named for the bristles around their heavy bills — relatives of toucans that chisel nest holes in trees and feast on fruit.

documents.name: Barn Owl
documents.description: The barn owl is a pale, heart-faced nocturnal bird of farmland and grassland, hunting voles by sound. Learn its habitat, diet, behavior, and conservation.

documents.name: Barnacle
documents.description: Explore barnacles (e.g. Semibalanus): sessile crustaceans that cement themselves head-down to rocks and shells and filter-feed with feathery legs from inside a shell.

documents.name: Barracuda
documents.description: Explore barracudas (genus Sphyraena): fast, streamlined predatory fish with fearsome jaws, from the large solitary great barracuda to species that form shimmering schools.

documents.name: Barreleye Fish
documents.description: Meet the barreleye fish (Macropinna microstoma), a small deep-sea fish with tubular green eyes inside a transparent, fluid-filled dome over its head.

documents.name: Basilisk
documents.description: Explore basilisks (genus Basiliscus): Central American lizards famous for sprinting across water on their hind legs — the 'Jesus Christ lizard' — using the green basilisk as a reference.

documents.name: Bat
documents.description: Bats are the only mammals capable of true flight. A group-level overview of order Chiroptera: echolocation, varied diets, roosting, and ecological importance.

documents.name: Batfish (Spadefish)
documents.description: Explore reef batfish (genus Platax): tall, flat, disc-shaped reef fish whose flowing-finned juveniles mimic leaves and flatworms — not to be confused with the deep-sea walking batfish.

documents.name: Bear
documents.description: An overview of bears (family Ursidae): the eight living species, their diverse diets and habitats, hibernation, and the conservation pressures across their range.

documents.name: Beaver
documents.description: Beavers are large, dam-building rodents and keystone wetland engineers. A group-level overview using the North American beaver as a reference species.

documents.name: Bee
documents.description: Bees are flying insects vital to pollination. A group-level overview using the honey bee as a reference species: flowers, diet, social and solitary species.

documents.name: Bee-eater
documents.description: Explore bee-eaters (family Meropidae): brilliantly coloured birds that catch bees and other flying insects in mid-air, with the European bee-eater as a dazzling reference species.

documents.name: Beetle
documents.description: Explore beetles (order Coleoptera): the most species-rich group of animals on Earth, with hardened wing cases, complete metamorphosis, and roles in almost every habitat.

documents.name: Bellbird
documents.description: Explore bellbirds (genus Procnias): Neotropical cotinga relatives whose males produce some of the loudest bird calls on Earth — clanging, bell-like notes — and sport bizarre fleshy wattles.

documents.name: Betta Fish
documents.description: The betta or Siamese fighting fish (Betta splendens): an educational profile of this labyrinth fish — appearance, native habitat, behaviour, and responsible aquarium context.

documents.name: Bichir
documents.description: Explore bichirs (genus Polypterus): ancient, armour-scaled African fish with a row of dorsal finlets and true lungs that let them gulp air — living relics of early ray-finned fishes.

documents.name: Bighorn Sheep
documents.description: Learn about the bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis), a wild sheep of western North American mountains, where rams carry massive, curling head-butting horns.

documents.name: Bilby
documents.description: Explore the greater bilby (Macrotis lagotis): a long-eared, burrowing desert marsupial of Australia — a vital ecosystem engineer, Vulnerable in the wild and an Easter icon.

documents.name: Binturong
documents.description: Explore the binturong (Arctictis binturong): a shaggy Southeast Asian viverrid with a prehensile tail that smells of popcorn — neither bear nor cat, and Vulnerable in the wild.

documents.name: Bird-of-Paradise
documents.description: Explore birds-of-paradise (family Paradisaeidae): New Guinea's spectacularly plumed birds whose males perform extravagant courtship displays — using the Raggiana bird-of-paradise.

documents.name: Bison
documents.description: Explore the American bison (Bison bison): North America's largest land mammal, its grassland habitat, grazing diet, herd behaviour, near-extinction, and conservation recovery.

documents.name: Black Dragonfish
documents.description: Meet the black dragonfish (genus Idiacanthus), a slender deep-sea predator with a glowing chin barbel, extreme sex differences, and stalk-eyed larvae.

documents.name: Black Swan
documents.description: The black swan (Cygnus atratus) is a large black waterbird with a red bill, native to wetlands in parts of Australia and introduced to New Zealand.

documents.name: Blenny
documents.description: Explore blennies (family Blenniidae): small, characterful reef and tide-pool fish with blunt heads, big eyes, and often feathery 'eyebrows' — including the mimic that copies the cleaner wrasse.

documents.name: Blue Morpho Butterfly
documents.description: Learn about the blue morpho butterfly, a large Neotropical insect known for iridescent blue wings produced by structural colour rather than pigment.

documents.name: Blue-Ringed Octopus
documents.description: Learn about blue-ringed octopuses (genus Hapalochlaena), small Indo-Pacific cephalopods famous for the iridescent blue rings they flash as a warning signal.

documents.name: Blue-tongued Skink
documents.description: Learn about blue-tongued skinks (genus Tiliqua), large short-legged lizards of parts of Australia and New Guinea named for their blue tongue display.

documents.name: Boa Constrictor
documents.description: Explore the boa constrictor (Boa constrictor): a large, non-venomous constricting snake of the Americas that kills prey by constriction and gives birth to live young.

documents.name: Boat-billed Heron
documents.description: Explore the boat-billed heron (Cochlearius cochlearius): a stocky, big-eyed nocturnal heron of American wetlands whose broad, boat-shaped bill scoops prey from the water in the dark.

documents.name: Bobcat
documents.description: Explore the bobcat (Lynx rufus): a medium-sized wild cat of North America, named for its short tail, and one of the continent's most adaptable predators.

documents.name: Bowerbird
documents.description: Explore bowerbirds (family Ptilonorhynchidae): Australasian birds whose males build and decorate elaborate 'bowers' to court females — one of the animal kingdom's great displays of art.

documents.name: Box Jellyfish
documents.description: Box jellyfish (class Cubozoa) are cube-bodied marine invertebrates with stinging tentacles, including Chironex fleckeri. Learn their biology and ecology.

documents.name: Box Turtle
documents.description: The box turtle (genus Terrapene) is a small North American turtle with a hinged shell that closes tight. Mostly land-dwelling; some populations declined.

documents.name: Boxfish
documents.description: Explore boxfish (family Ostraciidae): rigid, box-shaped reef fish encased in bony armour that swim with whirring fins — and can release a toxin into the water when stressed.

documents.name: Brain Coral
documents.description: Explore brain corals (e.g. Diploria): slow-growing stony corals whose maze-like, grooved surface resembles a brain — long-lived, boulder-shaped reef builders.

documents.name: Broadbill
documents.description: Explore broadbills (family Eurylaimidae): small, rounded, vividly coloured forest birds of Africa and Asia with broad gapes — some males make a remarkable whirring sound with their wings.

documents.name: Brown Bear
documents.description: The brown bear (Ursus arctos) is a single species whose regional populations include the grizzly and Kodiak bears. How to recognise it, where it lives, and what it eats.

documents.name: Brown Trout
documents.description: Learn about the brown trout (Salmo trutta), a variable European salmonid with resident and sea-run forms: its habitat, diet, ecology, and conservation.

documents.name: American Bullfrog
documents.description: Explore the American bullfrog (Lithobates catesbeianus): one of the largest North American frogs, a powerful, deep-voiced predator that is also invasive where introduced.

documents.name: Bumblebee
documents.description: Bumblebees (genus Bombus) are robust, hairy social bees known for buzz pollination and cold tolerance. Explore their ecology, foraging, and conservation.

documents.name: Burmese Python
documents.description: The Burmese python (Python bivittatus) is a large non-venomous constrictor native to South and Southeast Asia, and an introduced population in Florida.

documents.name: Bush Dog
documents.description: Meet the bush dog (Speothos venaticus): a short-legged, otter-like wild dog of Central and South America that hunts in packs near water and barely resembles a typical dog.

documents.name: Bustard
documents.description: Explore bustards (family Otididae): large, stately ground birds of open grasslands — among the heaviest flying birds — whose males perform spectacular puffed-up courtship displays.

documents.name: Butterfly
documents.description: Butterflies are day-flying insects with scaled wings and a four-stage life cycle. A group-level overview using the monarch as a reference: metamorphosis and diet.

documents.name: Butterflyfish
documents.description: Explore butterflyfish (family Chaetodontidae): disc-shaped, brilliantly patterned reef fish, often seen in faithful pairs, with many specialised to feed on living coral.

documents.name: Button-quail
documents.description: Meet the button-quail (Turnix): a small, secretive ground bird that looks like a quail but is not one — and in which the larger, bolder females court the males and leave them to raise the chicks.

documents.name: Caecilian
documents.description: Caecilians (order Gymnophiona) are limbless, mostly burrowing amphibians of wet tropics — not worms or snakes. Learn their biology, habitat, and ecology.

documents.name: Caiman
documents.description: Caimans are crocodilians of Central and South America. A group-level overview using the spectacled caiman as a reference — habitat, diet, and how caimans differ from alligators.

documents.name: Caiman Lizard
documents.description: Explore the caiman lizard (Dracaena guianensis): a large, semi-aquatic South American lizard with crocodile-like armoured scales and powerful jaws built for crushing snails.

documents.name: California Condor
documents.description: Learn about the California Condor, a critically endangered New World vulture and one of North America's largest flying birds, restored by captive breeding.

documents.name: Camel
documents.description: Explore camels (genus Camelus): the one-humped dromedary and two-humped Bactrian camel, their remarkable desert adaptations, diet, and long relationship with people.

documents.name: Cane Toad
documents.description: The cane toad (Rhinella marina) is a large toad native to the Americas and introduced to Australia, where it became a damaging invasive species.

documents.name: Western Capercaillie
documents.description: The Western Capercaillie is the largest grouse, a forest bird of parts of Europe and northern Asia known for its dramatic spring lekking displays.

documents.name: Capybara
documents.description: Explore the capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris): the world's largest rodent, a semi-aquatic, highly social grazer of South American wetlands and riverbanks.

documents.name: Caracal
documents.description: Explore the caracal (Caracal caracal): a sleek, tawny wild cat known for its long black ear tufts and a spectacular vertical leap used to snatch birds from the air.

documents.name: Northern Cardinal
documents.description: Explore the northern cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis): a vivid red North American songbird with a pointed crest, a familiar garden and woodland bird known for its clear whistled song.

documents.name: Carp
documents.description: The common carp (Cyprinus carpio): an educational profile of this widespread freshwater fish — habitat, omnivorous diet, behaviour, and its status as an introduced species.

documents.name: Carpenter Bee
documents.description: Carpenter bees (Xylocopa) are large, wood-nesting bees and buzz pollinators. Learn their habits, flower visits, nectar robbing, and cautious pollination role.

documents.name: Cassowary
documents.description: Explore the cassowary (genus Casuarius): a large, powerful flightless rainforest bird of New Guinea and northern Australia, known for its bony casque and vivid neck colours.

documents.name: Catfish
documents.description: Catfish are a huge group of barbel-bearing fish. A group-level overview using the channel catfish as a reference species: habitat, diet, behaviour, and aquarium context.

documents.name: Centipede
documents.description: Explore centipedes (class Chilopoda): fast, many-legged predatory arthropods with venomous claws — one pair of legs per body segment, unlike the millipedes they resemble.

documents.name: Chachalaca
documents.description: Explore chachalacas (genus Ortalis): slender, long-tailed Neotropical birds of the cracid family, named for their loud, raucous chorus — adaptable, sociable, and often heard at dawn.

documents.name: Chameleon
documents.description: Chameleons are colour-changing lizards with independently moving eyes. A group-level overview using the panther chameleon as a reference. Educational, not pet-care advice.

documents.name: Cheetah
documents.description: Acinonyx jubatus: the fastest land animal. Sprint-adapted anatomy, savanna habitats, diurnal hunting, the cheetah's slender build, and conservation pressures.

documents.name: Chicken
documents.description: The domestic chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus): its junglefowl ancestry, what combs and wattles do, why it dust bathes, how flock structure is described, and its precocial chicks.

documents.name: Chimpanzee
documents.description: Pan troglodytes: one of humans' closest living relatives. Forest habitats, omnivorous diet, tool use, complex social groups, and current conservation pressures.

documents.name: Chinchilla
documents.description: Group-level profile of the wild chinchillas of the high Andes: habitat, diet, behaviour, dense fur, and why the wild species are threatened while domestic chinchillas are common.

documents.name: Chinook Salmon
documents.description: Learn about the Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), the largest Pacific salmon, its anadromous life cycle, ecology, and varied conservation status.

documents.name: Chiton
documents.description: Chitons are marine mollusks of the class Polyplacophora, recognized by their eight overlapping shell plates. Learn their anatomy, habitat, diet, and behavior.

documents.name: Chorus Frog
documents.description: Meet the chorus frogs (Pseudacris): small striped North American tree frogs whose ringing breeding choruses are a classic sound of early spring — the group that includes the spring peeper.

documents.name: Chuckwalla
documents.description: Explore chuckwallas (genus Sauromalus): chunky, plant-eating desert lizards of North America that wedge into rock crevices and puff up to avoid being pulled out by predators.

documents.name: Cicada
documents.description: Explore cicadas (family Cicadidae): big-eyed insects famous for the males' loud buzzing song and for nymphs that live underground for years — including the periodical cicadas.

documents.name: Civet
documents.description: Explore civets (family Viverridae): cat-like nocturnal mammals of Africa and Asia, using the African civet as a reference — secretive omnivores with a distinctive scent gland.

documents.name: Clam
documents.description: Learn about clams, burrowing bivalve molluscs like the hard clam (quahog). Explore their shells, filter-feeding, habitat, and ecological role.

documents.name: African Clawed Frog
documents.description: Explore the African clawed frog (Xenopus laevis): a fully aquatic, tongueless African frog that became a famous lab animal and pregnancy test — and a problematic invader where released.

documents.name: Clouded Leopard
documents.description: Explore the clouded leopard (Neofelis nebulosa): a secretive Asian forest cat with cloud-shaped coat blotches, the longest canines for its size of any cat, and extraordinary climbing skills.

documents.name: Clownfish
documents.description: The clownfish or anemonefish (Amphiprion): an educational profile of these reef fish and their anemone partnership — habitat, behaviour, and marine-aquarium caution.

documents.name: Coati
documents.description: Explore coatis (genera Nasua & Nasuella): long-snouted, ring-tailed American mammals of the raccoon family, where females and young roam in lively, sociable bands.

documents.name: Cobra
documents.description: Explore cobras (genus Naja and relatives): venomous, hood-spreading elapid snakes of Africa and Asia, including the Indian cobra and king cobra, with a careful educational overview.

documents.name: Cock-of-the-Rock
documents.description: Explore the cock-of-the-rock (genus Rupicola): vivid orange or red South American birds whose males gather at leks to display — using the Andean cock-of-the-rock as a reference.

documents.name: Cockroach
documents.description: Explore cockroaches (order Blattodea): ancient, tough, fast insects — only a few are household pests, while most live in the wild as important recyclers of decaying matter.

documents.name: Coconut Crab
documents.description: Explore the coconut crab (Birgus latro): the largest land-living arthropod, a giant island hermit-crab relative with claws strong enough to crack coconuts.

documents.name: Cod
documents.description: Explore the Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua): a cold-water bottom fish of huge historical and economic importance, recognised by its chin barbel and once-vast North Atlantic stocks.

documents.name: Coelacanth
documents.description: Explore the coelacanth (Latimeria): a lobe-finned fish once thought extinct for tens of millions of years until it was found alive in 1938 — a deep-water living fossil and conservation priority.

documents.name: Colobus Monkey
documents.description: Explore colobus monkeys (genera Colobus and relatives): striking black-and-white African leaf monkeys with a reduced thumb and a leaf-fermenting stomach — graceful canopy leapers.

documents.name: Colugo (Flying Lemur)
documents.description: Explore colugos (order Dermoptera): Southeast Asian mammals that are the most accomplished gliders of all — neither lemurs nor fliers — using the Sunda colugo as a reference.

documents.name: Comb Jelly
documents.description: Explore comb jellies (phylum Ctenophora): shimmering, jellyfish-like ocean drifters that swim with rainbow-flickering 'comb' rows — not true jellyfish, and possibly the oldest animal branch.

documents.name: Commerson's Dolphin
documents.description: Explore Commerson's dolphin (Cephalorhynchus commersonii): a tiny, boldly black-and-white dolphin of cold southern waters — fast, playful, and highly social.

documents.name: Common Dolphin
documents.description: Explore the common dolphin (Delphinus delphis): a fast, acrobatic dolphin that forms huge, highly social pods — among the most intelligent and gregarious animals in the open ocean.

documents.name: Common Loon
documents.description: Learn about the Common Loon (Gavia immer), a diving waterbird of clear northern lakes known for its black-and-white plumage and haunting calls.

documents.name: Cone Snail
documents.description: Learn about cone snails (Conus), predatory tropical sea snails with patterned cone shells that hunt prey using a venomous harpoon-like tooth.

documents.name: Coral
documents.description: Explore corals (class Anthozoa): colonial cnidarian animals whose tiny polyps build reefs, partner with algae for energy, and underpin some of the richest habitats in the sea.

documents.name: Coral Snake
documents.description: Coral snakes (Micrurus and Micruroides) are banded, secretive New World elapids. A calm, educational overview of their biology, venom, mimicry, and ecology.

documents.name: Cotinga
documents.description: Explore cotingas (family Cotingidae): a diverse family of Neotropical birds famous for spectacular colours and bizarre displays — using the brilliant turquoise spangled cotinga.

documents.name: Coucal
documents.description: Meet the coucal (Centropus): a large, skulking ground cuckoo of the Old World that — unlike many cuckoos — builds its own nest and raises its own chicks rather than parasitising other birds.

documents.name: Cougar
documents.description: Learn about the cougar (Puma concolor), a large, solitary cat of the Americas also called puma and mountain lion: its range, diet, behavior, and ecology.

documents.name: Courser
documents.description: Explore coursers (family Glareolidae): long-legged, plover-like birds of dry open country that run swiftly across the ground rather than wade — relatives of the swallow-like pratincoles.

documents.name: Cow
documents.description: Domestic cattle (Bos taurus): an educational overview of the farm cow — herd behaviour, grazing diet, breeds, and the difference between domestic and wild bovines.

documents.name: Cowrie
documents.description: Cowries are marine sea snails (family Cypraeidae) with glossy, egg-shaped shells. Learn their biology, reef habitats, diet, and historic role as shell money.

documents.name: Coyote
documents.description: Explore the coyote (Canis latrans): a highly adaptable wild canid of North America that thrives from deserts and prairies to forests and cities.

documents.name: Crab
documents.description: Crabs are ten-legged crustaceans with a broad shell and pincers. A group-level overview of true crabs (Brachyura): habitats, diet, and sideways walking.

documents.name: Crabeater Seal
documents.description: The crabeater seal is a slender Antarctic pack-ice mammal that filters krill, not crabs. Learn its biology, habitat, and Least Concern status.

documents.name: Crayfish
documents.description: Explore crayfish (crawfish/yabbies): lobster-like freshwater crustaceans that clean up streams and ponds — clean-water indicators in some places, damaging invaders in others.

documents.name: Cricket
documents.description: Explore crickets (family Gryllidae): jumping insects famous for the males' chirping songs, made by rubbing their wings together — important in food webs, folklore, and even as food.

documents.name: Crocodile
documents.description: Crocodylidae: the true crocodiles. Tropical and subtropical aquatic predators across multiple continents. Anatomy, ambush hunting, and conservation context.

documents.name: Crow
documents.description: Crows are intelligent black birds in the genus Corvus. A group-level overview using the American crow as a reference: appearance, omnivorous diet, and behaviour.

documents.name: Crown-of-thorns Starfish
documents.description: Learn about the crown-of-thorns starfish, a native coral-feeding sea star of Indo-Pacific reefs, with notes on its ecology, outbreaks, and safety.

documents.name: Curassow
documents.description: Explore curassows (family Cracidae): big, crested, turkey-like birds of Neotropical forests — using the great curassow. Spectacular but heavily hunted, several are threatened.

documents.name: Cuscus
documents.description: Learn about the cuscus, slow-moving tree-dwelling marsupials of New Guinea and nearby areas, including their woolly fur, prehensile tail, diet and ecology.

documents.name: Cuttlefish
documents.description: Explore cuttlefish (order Sepiida): intelligent cephalopods that change colour and texture in an instant, hunt with lightning tentacles, and float using an internal cuttlebone.

documents.name: Damselfish
documents.description: Explore damselfish (family Pomacentridae): small, colourful, famously feisty reef fish — clownfish are among them — and some 'farm' and fiercely defend patches of algae on the coral.

documents.name: Damselfly
documents.description: A group-level profile of damselflies, suborder Zygoptera: wings held closed at rest, stalked wing bases, widely separated eyes, and nymphs with three external caudal gills.

documents.name: Deep-Sea Coral
documents.description: Deep-sea (cold-water) corals build reefs and gardens in cold, dark, deep water without sunlight, feeding on plankton and particles carried by currents.

documents.name: Deer
documents.description: An overview of deer (family Cervidae): white-tailed deer as a reference species, antlers, herbivorous browsing, social patterns, and human-impact context.

documents.name: Dhole
documents.description: Explore the dhole (Cuon alpinus): a rusty-red, pack-living Asiatic wild dog famous for whistling calls and cooperative hunts — an endangered predator of Asia's forests.

documents.name: Dik-dik
documents.description: Meet the dik-dik (Madoqua): a tiny African antelope with huge eyes and a flexible cooling snout, named for its alarm call and famous for living in monogamous pairs.

documents.name: Dingo
documents.description: Learn about the dingo, a wild canid of parts of mainland Australia, including its debated taxonomy, ecology, behaviour and conservation picture.

documents.name: Dolphin
documents.description: An overview of dolphins: family Delphinidae, social pods, echolocation, the common bottlenose dolphin as a reference species, and human-impact context.

documents.name: Donkey
documents.description: The donkey (Equus asinus) is a domesticated equid of dry, marginal country: long-eared, sure-footed and loud-voiced, and descended from the African wild ass, which survives in the wild only in tiny numbers.

documents.name: Douc
documents.description: Explore doucs (genus Pygathrix): vividly coloured leaf-eating monkeys of Southeast Asia, sometimes called the most beautiful primates — using the red-shanked douc. Endangered.

documents.name: Douroucouli (Night Monkey)
documents.description: Explore the douroucouli or night monkey (genus Aotus): the only truly nocturnal monkeys — big-eyed, pair-bonding primates of the American tropics where devoted fathers carry the young.

documents.name: Dragonet
documents.description: Explore dragonets (family Callionymidae): small, bottom-dwelling reef fish — including the dazzling mandarinfish, one of very few animals whose blue comes from true blue pigment.

documents.name: Dragonfly
documents.description: Dragonflies are fast-flying predatory insects with aquatic larvae. A group-level overview of Anisoptera: wetland habitats, hunting, and life cycle.

documents.name: Dromedary
documents.description: The dromedary (Camelus dromedarius) is the one-humped camel: a domesticated desert specialist with no wild population and large feral herds in Australia.

documents.name: Drongo
documents.description: Explore drongos (family Dicruridae): glossy black, fork-tailed birds of the Old World tropics — fierce nest-defenders and clever mimics that fake alarm calls to scare animals off their food.

documents.name: Duck
documents.description: Ducks are waterfowl in the family Anatidae. A group-level overview using the mallard as a reference species: wetland habitats, dabbling diet, and behaviour.

documents.name: Dugong
documents.description: The dugong (Dugong dugon) is a slow seagrass-grazing marine mammal of warm Indo-Pacific coastal waters. Learn its biology, ecology and IUCN status.

documents.name: Dumbo Octopus
documents.description: Explore the dumbo octopus (Grimpoteuthis): the deepest-living octopuses, named for the ear-like fins they flap to swim through the cold, dark ocean depths.

documents.name: Dung Beetle
documents.description: Dung beetles, of subfamily Scarabaeinae, roll, tunnel, and bury animal dung — recycling nutrients in African savannas and across most of the world.

documents.name: Eagle
documents.description: An overview of eagle species worldwide, using the Golden Eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) as the reference species for habitat, diet, flight, and conservation context.

documents.name: Earthworm
documents.description: Explore the earthworm (Lumbricus terrestris and relatives): segmented annelid worms that aerate and enrich soil, making them quiet but vital engineers of land ecosystems.

documents.name: Earwig
documents.description: Explore earwigs (order Dermaptera): nocturnal insects with rear pincers and a soft side — devoted mothers that guard their eggs — and the truth about the old myth that they crawl into ears.

documents.name: Echidna
documents.description: Explore echidnas (family Tachyglossidae): spiny, egg-laying mammals of Australia and New Guinea that, with the platypus, make up the unique monotreme group.

documents.name: Eel
documents.description: Eels are elongated, snake-like fish. A group-level overview of the order Anguilliformes using the moray eel as a reference: habitat, diet, life cycle, and caution.

documents.name: Electric Eel
documents.description: Explore the electric eel (Electrophorus electricus): an Amazonian knifefish — not a true eel — that generates powerful electric shocks to stun prey, navigate, and defend itself.

documents.name: Elephant
documents.description: An overview of African and Asian elephants: anatomy, range, herd structure, diet, and the conservation pressures facing the world's largest land mammals.

documents.name: Elk
documents.description: Explore the elk or wapiti (Cervus canadensis): one of the largest deer, famous for the bull's bugling call and massive antlers, across North America and parts of Asia.

documents.name: Elkhorn Coral
documents.description: Explore elkhorn coral (Acropora palmata): a large, flattened branching coral that once built Caribbean reef crests and now ranks among the most threatened corals.

documents.name: Emperor Penguin
documents.description: Learn about the emperor penguin, the largest living penguin: its sea-ice breeding, diet, biology, ecology and its IUCN conservation status.

documents.name: Emu
documents.description: Explore the emu (Dromaius novaehollandiae): Australia's largest bird, a tall flightless ratite of grassland and bush, second only to the ostrich in size.

documents.name: Eurasian Lynx
documents.description: Learn about the Eurasian lynx (Lynx lynx), the largest lynx species: its forest habitat, solitary hunting, ecology, and conservation across Eurasia.

documents.name: European Badger
documents.description: Learn about the European badger (Meles meles), a social, nocturnal mustelid with a striped face that lives in underground setts across parts of Europe.

documents.name: European Bison
documents.description: The European bison, or wisent (Bison bonasus), is Europe's largest wild land mammal. Explore its forest habitat, herbivorous diet, and remarkable recovery.

documents.name: European Eel
documents.description: Learn about the European eel, a catadromous, snake-like fish with a remarkable life cycle, its habitat, ecology, and Critically Endangered IUCN status.

documents.name: European Hare
documents.description: Learn about the European hare (Lepus europaeus), a large, fast-running lagomorph of grassland and farmland, and how this hare differs from rabbits.

documents.name: European Hedgehog
documents.description: The European hedgehog (Erinaceus europaeus) is a spiny nocturnal insectivore of gardens and hedgerows, now assessed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List.

documents.name: European Otter
documents.description: The European otter (Lutra lutra) is a semi-aquatic mustelid of rivers, wetlands and coasts. Learn its habitat, diet, ecology and Near Threatened status.

documents.name: European Tree Frog
documents.description: The European tree frog (Hyla arborea) is a small, bright-green climbing amphibian of waterside vegetation in parts of Europe, listed as Least Concern.

documents.name: European Adder
documents.description: Learn about the European adder (Vipera berus), a small venomous viper found across parts of Europe and Asia, including its appearance, habitat, and behavior.

documents.name: Fairy-wren
documents.description: Explore fairy-wrens (genus Malurus): tiny Australian songbirds with dazzling blue breeding males, cocked tails, cooperative family helpers — and famously unfaithful mating habits.

documents.name: Falcon
documents.description: An overview of falcons (family Falconidae): peregrine falcon as a reference species, high-speed aerial hunting, global distribution, and conservation context.

documents.name: Fennec Fox
documents.description: Explore the fennec fox (Vulpes zerda): the smallest fox in the world, a Sahara desert specialist whose huge ears shed heat and detect prey beneath the sand.

documents.name: Ferret
documents.description: Understand the ferret (Mustela putorius furo), the domesticated form of the European polecat: its long burrow-following body, obligate-carnivore biology, and how it differs from the wild black-footed ferret.

documents.name: Fiddler Crab
documents.description: Explore fiddler crabs (genus Uca and allies): small mudflat and mangrove crabs whose males wield one enormous claw, waved in courtship displays — and tireless recyclers of coastal mud.

documents.name: Fig Wasp
documents.description: Fig wasps (family Agaonidae) are tiny insects locked in an obligate mutualism with fig trees, pollinating figs while their larvae develop inside them.

documents.name: Fire-Bellied Toad
documents.description: Explore fire-bellied toads (genus Bombina): small Eurasian frogs that arch their backs to flash a vivid red-and-black belly — a warning of the toxins in their skin.

documents.name: Fire Salamander
documents.description: Explore the fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra): a striking black-and-yellow amphibian of European woodlands, known for its bold warning colours and moist forest life.

documents.name: Fishing Cat
documents.description: Explore the fishing cat (Prionailurus viverrinus): a stocky Asian wetland cat that swims, dives, and scoops fish from the water — a wetland specialist now threatened by habitat loss.

documents.name: Flamingo
documents.description: Flamingos are tall, pink, filter-feeding wading birds. A group-level overview using the greater flamingo as a reference: wetlands, diet, and why they are pink.

documents.name: Flat-headed Cat
documents.description: Discover the flat-headed cat (Prionailurus planiceps): a small, endangered wetland cat of Southeast Asia with a low flat head and part-webbed feet, adapted for catching fish and frogs.

documents.name: Flounder
documents.description: Explore flounders (flatfish, order Pleuronectiformes): seabed ambush fish that start life symmetrical and then have one eye migrate so both sit on top — masters of camouflage.

documents.name: Flying Fish
documents.description: Explore flying fish (family Exocoetidae): ocean fish that escape predators by launching out of the water and gliding on enlarged wing-like fins, sometimes for hundreds of metres.

documents.name: Flying Snake
documents.description: Explore flying snakes (genus Chrysopelea): Asian tree snakes that launch from branches and glide through the air by flattening their bodies into a ribbon — true gliders, not fliers.

documents.name: Fossa
documents.description: Explore the fossa (Cryptoprocta ferox): Madagascar's largest carnivore — a cat-like, lemur-hunting mammal related to mongooses, agile in the trees and Vulnerable in the wild.

documents.name: Fox
documents.description: An overview of true foxes (genus Vulpes), focusing on the red fox as a reference species: range, opportunistic diet, behaviour, and urban adaptation.

documents.name: Frigatebird
documents.description: Explore frigatebirds (family Fregatidae): huge-winged tropical seabirds where males inflate a scarlet throat pouch, that soar for days and steal food from other birds in mid-air.

documents.name: Frilled Lizard
documents.description: Explore the frilled lizard (Chlamydosaurus kingii): an Australian and New Guinean reptile that flares a huge neck frill and runs on two legs to bluff its way out of danger.

documents.name: Frilled Shark
documents.description: Explore the frilled shark (Chlamydoselachus anguineus): a rare, eel-like deep-sea shark with frilly gills and trident-shaped teeth, often called a living fossil.

documents.name: Frog
documents.description: Frogs (order Anura): tailless amphibians with a global distribution. Reference species the red-eyed tree frog, with cautious overview of biology and conservation.

documents.name: Frogfish
documents.description: Explore frogfish (family Antennariidae): lumpy, superbly camouflaged ambush predators that 'walk' on leg-like fins and dangle a built-in lure to fish for prey — with the fastest gape in the sea.

documents.name: Frogmouth
documents.description: Explore frogmouths (family Podargidae): nocturnal birds of Australasia that disguise themselves as broken branches by day — using the tawny frogmouth. Often mistaken for owls.

documents.name: Funnel-web Spider
documents.description: Australian funnel-web spiders (family Atracidae) live in burrows in parts of eastern and southern Australia. Calm, factual overview with a safety note.

documents.name: Galago (Bushbaby)
documents.description: Explore galagos or bushbabies (family Galagidae): small, wide-eyed nocturnal African primates that make spectacular leaps and call with eerie, baby-like cries.

documents.name: Galah
documents.description: Learn about the galah, a pink-and-grey cockatoo of much of mainland Australia. Covers its appearance, diet, behavior and IUCN Least Concern status.

documents.name: Galapagos Tortoise
documents.description: Learn about the Galapagos tortoise, a complex of giant tortoise species endemic to the Galapagos Islands, including its ecology, biology, and conservation.

documents.name: Gar
documents.description: Explore gars (family Lepisosteidae): long, armor-scaled, ancient predatory fish of the Americas that gulp air to breathe — using the giant alligator gar as a reference.

documents.name: Garter Snake
documents.description: Garter snakes (genus Thamnophis) are slender, harmless North American snakes often found near water. Learn their biology, diet, habitat, and conservation.

documents.name: Gecko
documents.description: Geckos are small lizards famous for climbing and vocalising. A group-level overview using the leopard gecko as a reference. Educational wildlife profile, not a care guide.

documents.name: Gelada
documents.description: Explore the gelada (Theropithecus gelada): a primate of the Ethiopian highlands that lives in huge herds, grazes on grass, and signals with a red 'bleeding-heart' chest patch.

documents.name: Genet
documents.description: Explore genets (genus Genetta): slender, spotted, cat-like carnivores of Africa and parts of Europe, agile nocturnal climbers with a long banded tail, using the common genet.

documents.name: Gerbil
documents.description: Gerbils are burrowing rodents of the subfamily Gerbillinae, adapted to arid and semi-arid country. A group-level profile, with the Mongolian gerbil as the familiar reference species.

documents.name: Gerenuk
documents.description: Explore the gerenuk (Litocranius walleri): an East African gazelle with a giraffe-like neck that rears up on its hind legs to browse high leaves — and can live without drinking water.

documents.name: Gharial
documents.description: Explore the gharial (Gavialis gangeticus): a critically endangered, fish-eating crocodilian of South Asian rivers, recognised by its extremely long, narrow snout.

documents.name: Giant Anteater
documents.description: Learn about the giant anteater, a large toothless mammal of Central and South America that eats ants and termites. Appearance, habitat, ecology and more.

documents.name: Giant Clam
documents.description: The giant clam (genus Tridacna) is the largest living bivalve. Learn how it grows on reefs, feeds via symbiotic algae, and why the man-eating myth is false.

documents.name: Giant Isopod
documents.description: Explore the giant isopod (Bathynomus): a large deep-sea crustacean and distant relative of woodlice, a seafloor scavenger that can survive long periods without food.

documents.name: Giant Otter
documents.description: The giant otter (Pteronura brasiliensis) is the largest otter, a social, fish-eating mammal of South American rivers and wetlands. IUCN Endangered.

documents.name: Giant Squid
documents.description: Explore the giant squid (Architeuthis dux): one of the largest invertebrates on Earth, a deep-ocean cephalopod with enormous eyes that was filmed alive in the wild only recently.

documents.name: Giant Weta
documents.description: Giant weta (genus Deinacrida) are very large flightless insects endemic to New Zealand. Explore their appearance, habitat, diet and conservation.

documents.name: Gibbon
documents.description: Explore gibbons (family Hylobatidae): the small, agile apes of Asian forests, famous for arm-swinging brachiation, loud songs, and strong pair bonds.

documents.name: Gila Monster
documents.description: Explore the Gila monster (Heloderma suspectum): a slow-moving, venomous desert lizard of the southwestern US and Mexico, with beaded skin, in a careful educational overview.

documents.name: Giraffe
documents.description: Giraffa: the tallest extant land animal. Anatomy of the long neck, savanna habitat, herbivorous browsing, social structure, and current conservation context.

documents.name: Girdled Lizard
documents.description: Explore girdled lizards (family Cordylidae): spiny, armour-plated African lizards — the armadillo girdled lizard rolls into a ball by biting its tail, like a tiny dragon.

documents.name: Glass Frog
documents.description: Explore glass frogs (family Centrolenidae): tiny Neotropical tree frogs with translucent undersides that reveal their organs, devoted fathers, and a remarkable transparency trick.

documents.name: Glass Lizard
documents.description: Explore glass lizards (e.g. Pseudopus apodus): snake-like legless lizards that shatter off their tail to escape — distinguished from true snakes by eyelids and ear openings.

documents.name: Glass Sponge
documents.description: Glass sponges (class Hexactinellida) build delicate skeletons of silica spicules. Meet the Venus' flower basket and these slow-growing deep-sea filter feeders.

documents.name: Go-away-bird
documents.description: Meet the go-away-bird (Corythaixoides): a grey, crested African turaco named for its loud nasal 'g'way' call, which warns other animals of approaching danger.

documents.name: Goat
documents.description: Domestic goat (Capra hircus): an educational overview of one of the earliest domesticated animals — browsing diet, agile climbing, herd behaviour, and farm context.

documents.name: Goby
documents.description: Explore gobies (family Gobiidae): one of the largest fish families — small bottom-dwellers with fused pelvic fins forming a suction disc, famous for partnerships like the goby and shrimp.

documents.name: Golden Eagle
documents.description: The Golden Eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) is a large dark-brown bird of prey of mountains and open uplands. Learn its diet, behavior, ecology and conservation.

documents.name: Goldfish
documents.description: The goldfish (Carassius auratus): an educational profile of this domesticated carp-family fish — varieties, behaviour, and why goldfish need far more space than a bowl.

documents.name: Goliath Birdeater
documents.description: Learn about the Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi), the world's largest spider by mass, a burrowing rainforest tarantula of northern South America.

documents.name: Goliath Frog
documents.description: Explore the goliath frog (Conraua goliath): the largest frog on Earth, a powerful river-dwelling amphibian of West-Central Africa that even builds its own nest ponds. Endangered.

documents.name: Goose
documents.description: Geese are large waterfowl in the family Anatidae. A group-level overview using the greylag goose as a reference species: grazing diet, flocking, and migration.

documents.name: Gorilla
documents.description: Gorilla: the largest living primate. Two species, western and eastern, group structure led by a silverback, herbivorous diet, and conservation status.

documents.name: Grass Snake
documents.description: The grass snake (Natrix natrix) is a non-venomous, water-loving European snake known for swimming, eating amphibians, and dramatic defensive bluffing.

documents.name: Grasshopper
documents.description: Explore grasshoppers (suborder Caelifera): plant-eating insects with powerful jumping legs that chirp, leap many times their length, and — in some species — swarm as locusts.

documents.name: Great White Shark
documents.description: Explore the great white shark (Carcharodon carcharias): the ocean's most famous large predatory fish — a powerful, warm-bodied hunter that is far less dangerous to people than its reputation suggests.

documents.name: Green Iguana
documents.description: The green iguana (Iguana iguana) is a large, mostly plant-eating arboreal lizard of the American tropics, with introduced populations in places like Florida.

documents.name: Green Sea Turtle
documents.description: The green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas) is a large marine turtle whose adults graze on seagrass and algae. Learn its biology, range, nesting, and IUCN status.

documents.name: Grouper
documents.description: Explore groupers (family Serranidae): large, heavy-bodied ambush predators of reefs and rocky bottoms, including the giant goliath grouper, with remarkable suction-feeding jaws.

documents.name: Guan
documents.description: Explore guans (family Cracidae): large, long-tailed Neotropical forest birds related to chachalacas and curassows — arboreal fruit-eaters and important seed dispersers.

documents.name: Guanaco
documents.description: Learn about the guanaco (Lama guanicoe), a wild South American camelid of the Andes and Patagonian steppe and the wild ancestor of the domestic llama.

documents.name: Guenon
documents.description: Explore guenons (genus Cercopithecus): a diverse group of strikingly marked African forest monkeys — using De Brazza's monkey, famous for its white beard and orange brow.

documents.name: Guinea Pig
documents.description: Cavia porcellus: the guinea pig as a companion animal. Origin, social behaviour, herbivorous diet, vitamin C requirement, and responsible-ownership guidance.

documents.name: Gulper Eel
documents.description: Meet the gulper eel (Eurypharynx pelecanoides), or pelican eel, a deep-sea fish with an enormous expandable mouth and slender whip-like tail.

documents.name: Guppy
documents.description: The guppy (Poecilia reticulata): an educational profile of this small, colourful livebearing fish — appearance, native range, behaviour, and responsible aquarium context.

documents.name: Hagfish
documents.description: Explore hagfish (class Myxini): ancient, jawless, eel-shaped deep-sea fish that defend themselves by instantly producing huge amounts of slime, and tie themselves in knots to feed.

documents.name: Hamerkop
documents.description: Explore the hamerkop (Scopus umbretta): a brown African wading bird with a hammer-shaped head that builds one of the largest, most elaborate nests of any bird.

documents.name: Hammerhead Shark
documents.description: Explore hammerhead sharks (family Sphyrnidae): predatory sharks with a wide, flattened head that improves their senses — including the great hammerhead, a powerful ray hunter.

documents.name: Hamster
documents.description: Hamsters as pets and in the wild: Syrian hamster reference species, nocturnal solitary biology, omnivorous diet, and species-appropriate housing.

documents.name: Harpy Eagle
documents.description: The harpy eagle is one of the largest, most powerful raptors of lowland tropical rainforest in parts of Central and South America. An educational profile.

documents.name: Hatchetfish
documents.description: Marine hatchetfish (family Sternoptychidae) are small, silvery deep-sea fish with belly light organs that hide their silhouette through counterillumination.

documents.name: Hawk
documents.description: Hawks are sharp-eyed birds of prey. A group-level overview using the red-tailed hawk as a reference: hunting, habitat, and how hawks relate to other raptors.

documents.name: Hawk Moth
documents.description: Hawk moths (family Sphingidae) are fast, hovering moths with long tongues. Learn how some act as important nocturnal pollinators of long-tubed flowers.

documents.name: Hawkfish
documents.description: Explore hawkfish (family Cirrhitidae): small reef predators that perch on coral with thickened fins and dart out to seize prey — including the lattice-patterned longnose hawkfish.

documents.name: Hedgehog
documents.description: Hedgehogs are small spiny insectivores. A group-level overview using the European hedgehog as a reference species: spines, diet, and nocturnal behaviour.

documents.name: Hellbender
documents.description: Explore the hellbender (Cryptobranchus alleganiensis): North America's largest salamander, a fully aquatic 'snot otter' that breathes through its skin and signals clean rivers.

documents.name: Hermit Crab
documents.description: Explore hermit crabs (superfamily Paguroidea): soft-bellied crustaceans that protect themselves in empty snail shells and trade up as they grow — sometimes in an orderly housing chain.

documents.name: Heron
documents.description: Explore herons (family Ardeidae): tall, long-legged wading birds that hunt fish and other prey at the water's edge, with the grey heron as a familiar reference species.

documents.name: Hippopotamus
documents.description: Explore Hippopotamus amphibius: where hippos live across sub-Saharan Africa, their semi-aquatic life, grazing diet, social pods, and conservation context.

documents.name: Hoatzin
documents.description: Explore the hoatzin (Opisthocomus hoazin): a strange crested Amazonian bird that digests leaves by fermentation like a cow — and whose chicks have claws on their wings.

documents.name: Honeyeater
documents.description: Honeyeaters (family Meliphagidae) are Australasian nectar-feeding birds with brush-tipped tongues that can pollinate native plants like eucalypts, banksias.

documents.name: Honeyguide
documents.description: Explore honeyguides (family Indicatoridae): African and Asian birds that famously lead humans to bees' nests to share the spoils — and that, like cuckoos, lay their eggs in other birds' nests.

documents.name: Hoopoe
documents.description: Explore the Eurasian hoopoe (Upupa epops): an unmistakable pinkish-brown bird with a fan-like crest, barred wings, and a long curved bill for probing the ground for insects.

documents.name: Hornbill
documents.description: Explore hornbills (family Bucerotidae): large tropical birds of Africa and Asia known for their big down-curved bills, casques, and remarkable sealed-nest breeding.

documents.name: Horned Lizard
documents.description: Explore horned lizards (genus Phrynosoma): flat, spiny desert reptiles of the Americas — ant specialists famous for camouflage and squirting blood from their eyes to deter predators.

documents.name: Hornero
documents.description: Explore horneros (genus Furnarius): South American 'ovenbirds' famous for building sturdy domed mud nests shaped like old clay ovens — using the rufous hornero, Argentina's national bird.

documents.name: Horse
documents.description: Equus caballus: domestic horse profile covering origin, body plan, social behaviour, diet, and the modern relationship between horses and humans.

documents.name: Horseshoe Crab
documents.description: Explore horseshoe crabs (family Limulidae): ancient marine arthropods — not true crabs — that have barely changed in hundreds of millions of years, with blue blood vital to medicine.

documents.name: Hoverfly
documents.description: Hoverflies (family Syrphidae) are true flies that mimic bees and wasps but cannot sting. Learn how these flower flies visit blooms and pollinate.

documents.name: Howler Monkey
documents.description: Explore howler monkeys (genus Alouatta): among the loudest land animals, New World monkeys whose dawn roars carry for kilometres, with a strong prehensile tail and a leafy diet.

documents.name: Hummingbird
documents.description: Hummingbirds are tiny, fast-flying nectar specialists. A group-level overview using Anna's hummingbird as a reference: hovering flight, diet, and behaviour.

documents.name: Hummingbird Hawk-moth
documents.description: The hummingbird hawk-moth (Macroglossum stellatarum) is a day-flying moth that hovers at flowers like a hummingbird. A nectar feeder and flower visitor.

documents.name: Humpback Whale
documents.description: Learn about the humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae), a large baleen whale known for long migrations, breaching and complex songs across world oceans.

documents.name: Hydrothermal Vent Tubeworm
documents.description: The giant tube worm (Riftia pachyptila) thrives around deep-sea hydrothermal vents, feeding via chemosynthetic bacteria with no mouth or gut.

documents.name: Hyena
documents.description: Hyenas are intelligent, social carnivores of Africa and Asia. A group-level overview using the spotted hyena as a reference — habitat, diet, behaviour, and ecological role.

documents.name: Icefish
documents.description: Icefish (family Channichthyidae) are Southern Ocean fish that lack haemoglobin and have nearly colourless, white blood. Explore their biology.

documents.name: Iguana
documents.description: The green iguana (Iguana iguana) and its relatives: an educational profile of these large, mostly herbivorous lizards — appearance, range, behaviour, and wild vs pet context.

documents.name: Indri
documents.description: Explore the indri (Indri indri): the largest living lemur, a tail-less leaping primate of Madagascar famous for its haunting whale-like songs. Critically Endangered.

documents.name: Jabiru
documents.description: Explore the jabiru (Jabiru mycteria): a huge stork of Central and South American wetlands with a black neck and red band — among the tallest flying birds in the Americas.

documents.name: Jacamar
documents.description: Explore jacamars (family Galbulidae): slender, iridescent Neotropical birds with long needle-like bills that catch butterflies and other flying insects in dazzling aerial sallies.

documents.name: Jacana
documents.description: Explore jacanas (family Jacanidae): tropical wetland birds with enormous toes that let them walk on floating plants — and famous for sex-role-reversed breeding where males raise the young.

documents.name: Jaguar
documents.description: Panthera onca: the largest big cat in the Americas. Distribution from Mexico to South America, ambush hunting, exceptional bite force, and conservation context.

documents.name: Jaguarundi
documents.description: Explore the jaguarundi (Herpailurus yagouaroundi): an unusual, weasel-like American wild cat with a long body, short legs, and a plain coat — active by day and surprisingly vocal.

documents.name: Jellyfish
documents.description: Jellyfish are soft-bodied, drifting marine animals with stinging tentacles. A group-level overview using the moon jelly as a reference: anatomy, diet, and caution.

documents.name: Kagu
documents.description: Explore the kagu (Rhynochetos jubatus): a near-flightless, ash-grey forest bird found only in New Caledonia, with a loud dawn call and 'nasal corns' unique among birds. Endangered.

documents.name: Kakapo
documents.description: Explore the kakapo (Strigops habroptilus): the world's heaviest parrot — a flightless, nocturnal, critically endangered New Zealand bird saved by intensive conservation.

documents.name: Kangaroo
documents.description: Macropus / Osphranter: Australian marsupial macropods. Hopping locomotion, mobs, herbivorous grazing, pouch-rearing biology, and modern conservation context.

documents.name: Kea
documents.description: Explore the kea (Nestor notabilis): the world's only alpine parrot — a famously intelligent, curious, and mischievous mountain bird of New Zealand's South Island.

documents.name: King Cobra
documents.description: Learn about the king cobra (Ophiophagus hannah), the world's longest venomous snake, found in forests across parts of South and Southeast Asia.

documents.name: King Vulture
documents.description: Learn about the King Vulture, a striking New World vulture of Central and South American forests, with its multicoloured head and scavenging habits.

documents.name: Kingfisher
documents.description: Explore kingfishers (family Alcedinidae): small, vivid, big-headed birds famous for diving to catch fish, with the common kingfisher as a brilliant reference species.

documents.name: Kinkajou
documents.description: Explore the kinkajou (Potos flavus): a golden, nocturnal rainforest mammal of the Americas with a grasping tail and a sweet tooth for fruit and nectar — and a role as a pollinator.

documents.name: Kiwi
documents.description: Explore kiwi (genus Apteryx): the small, flightless, nocturnal birds found only in New Zealand, famous for their long bills, hair-like feathers, and unusually large eggs.

documents.name: Koala
documents.description: Phascolarctos cinereus: Australia's eucalyptus-specialist marsupial. Tree-dwelling lifestyle, slow metabolism, conservation pressures including disease and fire.

documents.name: Kodkod
documents.description: Meet the kodkod or guiña (Leopardus guigna): the smallest wild cat in the Americas, a spotted forest hunter of Chile and Argentina, where dark (melanistic) individuals are common.

documents.name: Koi
documents.description: Koi are ornamental varieties of the common carp kept in ponds. An educational profile: colours, pond habitat, behaviour, and why koi are a long-term commitment.

documents.name: Komodo Dragon
documents.description: The Komodo dragon (Varanus komodoensis): an educational profile of the world's largest living lizard — its Indonesian range, diet, behaviour, and conservation context.

documents.name: Kookaburra
documents.description: Explore the kookaburra (genus Dacelo): large Australasian kingfishers famous for their loud, laughing call, with the laughing kookaburra as the best-known species.

documents.name: Krait
documents.description: Explore kraits (genus Bungarus): highly venomous, mostly nocturnal Asian snakes — using the banded krait. An educational profile that is not first-aid or medical advice.

documents.name: Krill
documents.description: Explore krill (order Euphausiacea): small, shrimp-like crustaceans that swarm in vast numbers and feed whales, seals, penguins, and fish — a keystone of ocean food webs.

documents.name: Lacewing
documents.description: Explore lacewings (order Neuroptera): delicate, lacy-winged insects whose voracious larvae — nicknamed 'aphid lions' — are prized natural pest controllers in gardens and farms.

documents.name: Ladybug
documents.description: Ladybugs (ladybirds) are small beetles, many of them helpful predators of aphids. A group-level overview of Coccinellidae: appearance, diet, and garden benefit.

documents.name: Lake Sturgeon
documents.description: Discover the lake sturgeon, an ancient, slow-growing freshwater fish of North America with bony scutes, barbels, a shark-like tail, and long lifespan.

documents.name: Lamprey
documents.description: Explore lampreys (order Petromyzontiformes): ancient, eel-shaped jawless fish with a round, toothed sucker mouth — some parasitic, all part of a 350-million-year-old lineage.

documents.name: Lancelet
documents.description: Meet the lancelet (Branchiostoma): a small, translucent, fish-shaped marine animal — not a fish and not a vertebrate — that is one of the closest living relatives of the backboned animals.

documents.name: Langur
documents.description: Explore langurs (leaf monkeys of the subfamily Colobinae): slender, long-tailed Asian monkeys that ferment leaves to digest them — using the sacred gray langur as a reference.

documents.name: Lanternfish
documents.description: Meet the lanternfish (Myctophidae): small, light-producing deep-sea fish that may be among the most abundant vertebrates on Earth and migrate up to the surface and back down every night.

documents.name: Leafcutter Ant
documents.description: Learn about the leafcutter ant (Atta and Acromyrmex), Neotropical insects that cut leaves to farm fungus in vast underground colonies across the Americas.

documents.name: Leafcutter Bee
documents.description: Leafcutter bees (Megachile, family Megachilidae) are solitary bees that cut leaf discs to line nests and carry pollen on belly hairs. Not the leafcutter ant.

documents.name: Leafhopper
documents.description: Meet the leafhoppers (Cicadellidae): a huge family of small, often colourful sap-sucking insects that jump powerfully, coat themselves in water-repelling 'brochosomes', and include many crop pests.

documents.name: Leafy Seadragon
documents.description: The leafy seadragon (Phycodurus eques) is a small marine fish of southern and western Australian waters, famous for its leaf-like camouflage.

documents.name: Leatherback Sea Turtle
documents.description: The leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) is the largest living turtle: a deep-diving, jellyfish-eating marine reptile with a leathery, ridged shell.

documents.name: Leech
documents.description: Learn about leeches (subclass Hirudinea), segmented worms related to earthworms, including the well-known medicinal leech, with calm, factual notes.

documents.name: Legless Lizard
documents.description: Explore legless lizards (e.g. Anniella, and Australia's flap-footed lizards): limbless, snake-like lizards that 'swim' through sand — told apart from snakes by eyelids and ear openings.

documents.name: Lemur
documents.description: Lemurs are primates found only on Madagascar. A group-level overview using the ring-tailed lemur as a reference — habitat, diet, social behaviour, and conservation concern.

documents.name: Leopard
documents.description: Panthera pardus: the most widely distributed big cat. Habitat adaptability, solitary lifestyle, ambush hunting, and the conservation pressures across its range.

documents.name: Leopard Seal
documents.description: Learn about the leopard seal, a large Southern Ocean predator of Antarctic pack ice that takes penguins, seals, fish, and krill. IUCN Least Concern.

documents.name: Limpet
documents.description: Limpets are marine gastropod molluscs with simple cone-shaped shells that cling to wave-battered rocks, graze algae, and live on rocky shores worldwide.

documents.name: Limpkin
documents.description: Explore the limpkin (Aramus guarauna): a brown, white-flecked American wetland bird with a curved bill specialised for extracting apple snails, famous for its eerie wailing cry.

documents.name: Lion
documents.description: Explore Panthera leo: where lions live across Africa and India, how pride social structures work, what lions hunt, and key conservation context.

documents.name: Lionfish
documents.description: Explore the lionfish (genus Pterois): a striking reef predator with venomous spines, native to the Indo-Pacific and a notorious invasive species in the western Atlantic and Caribbean.

documents.name: Llama
documents.description: Learn about the llama (Lama glama), a domesticated South American camelid descended from the wild guanaco, long used in the Andes for transport and wool.

documents.name: Lobster
documents.description: Lobsters are large seabed crustaceans with powerful claws. A group-level overview using the American lobster as a reference species: habitat, diet, and moulting.

documents.name: Longhorn Beetle
documents.description: Longhorn beetles (family Cerambycidae) are long-antennaed wood-borers; some flower-visiting lineages feed on pollen and nectar and can act as pollinators.

documents.name: Luna Moth
documents.description: Learn about the luna moth (Actias luna), a large pale green silk moth of eastern North American forests, with long trailing tails and a brief adult life.

documents.name: Lungfish
documents.description: Explore lungfish (subclass Dipnoi): ancient 'living fossil' fish that breathe air with true lungs, and whose African species can survive months out of water in a mud cocoon.

documents.name: Lynx
documents.description: Lynx are medium-sized wild cats with tufted ears and short tails. A group-level overview using the Eurasian lynx as a reference species: forest habitat and hunting.

documents.name: Lyrebird
documents.description: Explore the superb lyrebird (Menura novaehollandiae): an Australian songbird famed for jaw-dropping vocal mimicry and an ornate lyre-shaped tail used in courtship.

documents.name: Macaque
documents.description: Explore macaques (genus Macaca): among the most adaptable and widespread monkeys — using the Japanese macaque (snow monkey), famous for bathing in hot springs.

documents.name: Macaw
documents.description: Macaws are large, long-tailed Neotropical parrots of Central and South America. Learn their appearance, ecology, and varying conservation status.

documents.name: Mackerel
documents.description: Explore mackerel (e.g. Atlantic mackerel, Scomber scombrus): fast, streamlined schooling fish of the open sea, marked with wavy bars and central to ocean food webs and fisheries.

documents.name: Magpie
documents.description: Explore the magpie (Pica pica and relatives): a bold, intelligent black-and-white corvid of Eurasia and North America, known for its long tail and resourceful behaviour.

documents.name: Mahseer
documents.description: Learn about the mahseer, large freshwater carp of the genus Tor found in fast-flowing rivers across parts of South and Southeast Asia, and its conservation.

documents.name: Mamba
documents.description: Explore mambas (genus Dendroaspis): fast, alert, highly venomous African snakes — using the black mamba as a reference. Shy by nature and ecologically important predators.

documents.name: Manakin
documents.description: Explore manakins (family Pipridae): small, brightly marked Neotropical birds whose males perform astonishing courtship dances — including 'moonwalks' and mechanical wing sounds.

documents.name: Mandarin Duck
documents.description: Learn about the mandarin duck (Aix galericulata), an ornate East Asian perching duck. Explore its appearance, woodland-pond habitat, diet, and cultural meaning.

documents.name: Mandrill
documents.description: Explore the mandrill (Mandrillus sphinx): the largest monkey, a forest-dwelling African primate famous for the male's brilliant red-and-blue face and huge social groups. Vulnerable.

documents.name: Maned Wolf
documents.description: Explore the maned wolf (Chrysocyon brachyurus): a tall, long-legged South American canid — neither wolf nor fox — that eats lots of fruit and marks with a famously skunky scent.

documents.name: Mantella
documents.description: Explore mantellas (genus Mantella): tiny, brilliantly coloured toxic frogs of Madagascar — a striking parallel to South America's poison dart frogs. Several are Endangered.

documents.name: Mantis Shrimp
documents.description: Explore mantis shrimp (order Stomatopoda): dazzlingly coloured marine crustaceans with one of the fastest, most powerful strikes in nature and possibly the most complex eyes of any animal.

documents.name: Marabou Stork
documents.description: Learn about the marabou stork (Leptoptilos crumenifer), a huge bare-headed African stork that scavenges carrion across parts of sub-Saharan Africa.

documents.name: Marbled Newt
documents.description: Explore the marbled newt (Triturus marmoratus): a striking green-and-black newt of western Europe that breeds in ponds and spends much of the year hidden on land.

documents.name: Margay
documents.description: Explore the margay (Leopardus wiedii): a small, large-eyed spotted cat of the American tropics — an exceptional climber with ankles that rotate, letting it descend trees head-first.

documents.name: Marine Iguana
documents.description: Learn about the marine iguana, a lizard endemic to the Galapagos Islands that grazes on algae underwater, basks on lava rocks, and "sneezes" out salt.

documents.name: Markhor
documents.description: Explore the markhor (Capra falconeri): a large wild goat of Central and South Asia with magnificent corkscrew horns — Pakistan's national animal and a major conservation success story.

documents.name: Marmoset
documents.description: Explore marmosets (family Callitrichidae): tiny South American monkeys that gnaw tree bark to feed on gum, usually give birth to twins, and live in cooperative family groups.

documents.name: Mason Bee
documents.description: Mason bees (Osmia spp.) are gentle, solitary cavity-nesting bees that seal nests with mud. Learn how these early-spring flower visitors live and pollinate.

documents.name: Mayfly
documents.description: Explore mayflies (order Ephemeroptera): ancient winged insects whose adults live only hours to days, while the long-lived nymphs are key indicators of healthy fresh water.

documents.name: Meerkat
documents.description: The meerkat (Suricata suricatta) is a small, highly social mongoose of southern Africa. An educational profile of its desert habitat, cooperative behaviour, and diet.

documents.name: Mekong Giant Catfish
